items.title: [News] NVIDIA’s 1st Earnings Without Huang: Comeback Ruled Out; Memory, Packaging Secured as TSMC Helps Ease Supply Gap
items.author: N/A
items.highlights: As rivals including AMD and ASIC developers vie for capacity amid NVIDIA’s leadership turmoil, the AI chip giant is moving to shore up its supply chain. According to Commercial Times, TSMC executives visited NVIDIA this week to help bridge the supply-demand gap, while Kress reaffirmed that memory and advanced packaging capacity had been secured. NVIDIA also unveiled new agreements with Kinsus and SPIL to expand ABF substrate and advanced packaging capacity, respectively. items.title: AI, data center demand drive Nvidia revenue to $115.8B in Q3 | Manufacturing Dive
items.author: Jeff Kinney
items.highlights: ### Dive Brief: - Nvidia Nov. 17 reported revenue of $115.8 billion in its fiscal third quarter of 2027 ending Oct. 25, up from $57 billion year over year. Growth was driven in large part by artificial intelligence and data center demand. - On an earnings call, the company announced expanded long-term commitments with supply chain partners to support artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.
